source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting results that contradict the hypothesis in a psychology research report

1. Start with the research records.
2.
completion:
Begin by meticulously detailing all of the steps you took throughout your study, starting from the design phase to execution. Document any exploratory or secondary analyses that were conducted in addition to the main hypothesis tests. Clearly outline the operational definitions and measurements, so that other researchers could potentially reproduce the study. 

3. Present the data.
Clearly describe the raw and processed data, using charts, tables, or graphs when appropriate. This should include how missing data was handled, any transformations performed on the variables, and the rationale for these decisions. Visual representations can often convey the findings more effectively than just text.

4. Report the analyses used.
Outline the statistical methods used and justify their selection. Whether you employed t-tests, ANOVAs, regression analyses, or other statistical tools, ensure you relay how you chose the correct methods to answer your research questions.
